title: I found AI gaming channels running 24/7 livestreams making up to $27K/month
author: saikiranbali
selftext:
Recently I came across something pretty interesting while researching YouTube gaming streams.

There are some channels running 24/7 gaming livestreams where the gameplay is actually controlled by AI. The creator doesn’t really play the game themselves. Instead, the system runs automated gameplay and streams it continuously.

One example I found is a channel called FlagBattle.

According to analytics tools, some of these channels are estimated to make anywhere between $9K and $27K per month from YouTube ads.

Another interesting part is how they keep viewers engaged. The stream integrates with YouTube live chat using APIs, so viewers can comment during the stream and influence what happens in the game.

Because people keep interacting through chat, the livestream stays active and engaging for long periods of time.

I made a short breakdown showing one of these channels and the estimated earnings:

[https://youtube.com/shorts/1QejzL09\_tQ](https://youtube.com/shorts/1QejzL09_tQ)

I'm curious if anyone here has experimented with this type of automated streaming setup or knows more about how these channels are running their systems.

replies.author: saikiranbali
replies.body:
Yeah that’s a good point. I think these streams rely on a different type of engagement loop compared to traditional games.

It’s less about deep gameplay and more about quick interaction and social participation. When viewers type something in chat and immediately see it affect the stream (spawning, attacking, voting, etc.), it creates a feedback loop that keeps people commenting.

It’s similar to things like Twitch Plays or chat-controlled streams where the fun is more in the collective chaos and participation rather than the game mechanics themselves.

Now it’s up to your creativity how to keep them engaging.

replies.author: SKNRSN
replies.body:
Socialblade shows false stats when it comes to the monetization. Livestream CPM rates are very low compared to the normal views. Most views come from countries with bad CPM rates. 

Socialblade shows that the channel you've shown on your video has 4 million views in total; For it to make $9K (the lowest value from your bracket) it would need to have 2.25$ CPM. That kind of CPM is impossible for a livestream on youtube for the type of audience that watches this.

Sites that estimate revenue always asume that the channel is in high-paying niche, has long-form videos and has audience from USA.
